mutants.reason: The AND of RESP and ERR states is never true, so beats_left and the read address never advance and multi-beat reads return the wrong beat count, RLAST and addresses.
WDATA/WSTRB are captured and beats_left decremented in the wrong states, so PWDATA/PSTRB and the W beat count are wrong.
A 1 in the top bit makes the end-page compare always unequal, so every write is flagged as 4-KiB crossing and rejected with SLVERR and no APB access.
AWREADY and wr_ready are asserted in every state except IDLE, so an AW is accepted at the wrong time and a write is not accepted in IDLE.
The WRAP wrap-detect compare is inverted, so WRAP write beat addresses do not wrap at the boundary and are wrong.
req_ready is asserted only when the APB FSM is not idle, so the payload is never captured in IDLE. The APB transfer runs with stale zero payload and the sequencers advance early.
The response (PRDATA/PSLVERR capture and rsp_valid pulse) is generated outside the ACCESS state, so the AXI completion is lost or wrong and the transaction hangs.
With OR, W data is captured and beats_left decremented whenever WVALID is high in any state, or every cycle in WDAT. The beat count, PWDATA and PSTRB are corrupted.

This is the default assignment at the top of the always_comb. The following case on the APB state overwrites o_apb_pwrite in every branch: SETUP and ACCESS set it from reg_apb_wr, and the default branch sets it to 0. The initial value never reaches the port.
w_ar_valid defaults to 0 and nothing sets it to 1, so every read, including legal ones, is rejected with SLVERR and no APB access.
A write is captured as a read: PWRITE=0 with non-zero PSTRB/PWDATA, and the response goes down the read path, so the write is not performed and BRESP is lost.
RVALID defaults to 1 and is never cleared in IDLE/REQ/WAIT, so RVALID is high in reset and spurious R beats appear.

The OR becomes an AND, so the result differs only for a WRAP burst with exactly one fault: a bad length (not 2/4/8/16) with an aligned address, or a good length with a misaligned address. Both are illegal AXI4 WRAP bursts, so they are outside the legal stimulus. The assumptions say the response class for them is unspecified and they are never generated. Every legal WRAP burst gives identical outputs.

The mutant clears reg_turn_rd while in ACTRD even without rd_done. The value is used only in the IDLE state, and ACTRD always ends with rd_done, which clears it anyway. rd_done can only be high while the owner state is ACTRD. Reset still sets it to 1, so the port-visible arbitration is identical.
Requiring both a read and a write grant at once is never true, so the APB FSM never leaves IDLE and no APB transfer starts.
beats_left and the address advance only on the last beat instead of on every non-last beat, so beat addresses and RLAST are wrong for bursts longer than one beat.
req_valid is asserted in every state except REQ, so a spurious APB request is raised in IDLE/ERR/RESP, including for unsupported reads, and the REQ state never requests.
The valid/invalid branch is swapped: legal reads go to the ERR path with SLVERR and no APB, and unsupported reads go to the APB path.
rd_done fires on RLAST alone without RREADY, so ownership is released before the final R handshake and a new request can be accepted while R is stalled.
BVALID is never asserted in BRESP, so no B response is returned and the write hangs.

The OR becomes an AND, so the result differs only for a WRAP read with exactly one fault: a bad length with an aligned address, or a good length with a misaligned address. Both are illegal AXI4 WRAP bursts, so they are outside the legal stimulus. The assumptions say the response class for them is unspecified and they are never generated. Every legal WRAP burst gives identical outputs.
AWREADY and wr_ready are asserted in every state except IDLE, so an AW is accepted at the wrong time and a write is not accepted in IDLE.
The INCR beat count used for the 4-KiB check is inflated by 256, so legal INCR writes are falsely flagged as crossing and rejected with SLVERR.
req_valid is asserted in every state except REQ, including DRAIN, so an unsupported write makes APB accesses. The REQ state never requests, so legal writes stall.
The cache check is inverted: AWCACHE=0000 is rejected, while the other illegal cache values such as 0010 are accepted and written to APB.
The arbitration preference is inverted, so a first AR/AW tie after reset is won by AW and the alternation is reversed.

The request payload (address, direction, PROT, data, strobe) is captured only when the APB FSM is not IDLE, which never coincides with req_ready, so it is never captured. APB drives stale zero values.
The write error flag is set whenever the stale i_rsp_err is high, even outside WAIT. An earlier error response can leak into a later error-free write and give a wrong SLVERR BRESP.
PENABLE defaults to 1 in the idle branch, so PENABLE is high while PSEL=0, including after reset.
rd_ready is never asserted in IDLE, so the owner FSM never moves from GRD to ACTRD and reads are never accepted into service.
PSEL is 0 during ACCESS, so the access phase is never selected: PENABLE=1 with PSEL=0, and the completer is never accessed.
The INCR beat count used for the 4-KiB check is inflated by 256, so legal INCR reads are falsely flagged as crossing and rejected with SLVERR.
WREADY needs both WDAT and DRAIN at once, so it is never asserted and no W beat is accepted, which hangs the write.
The APB FSM leaves IDLE on o_gnt_rd alone, before the read request is valid, so a spurious APB transfer starts with stale payload. This includes reads that will be rejected.
The cache check is inverted: ARCACHE=0000 is rejected, while the other illegal cache values are accepted and issued to APB.
The condition is true in every state except ERR, so RVALID/RLAST are asserted in IDLE/REQ/WAIT (including in reset) and are low in the ERR state, so unsupported reads return no SLVERR beats.
